candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — assess risk factors and reinforce age- and risk-appropriate preventive screening
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — risk-based screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes
candidate.educational_objective: Apply risk-based diabetes screening by testing asymptomatic adults before age 35 when overweight or obesity is accompanied by additional recognized risk factors such as first-degree family history or physical inactivity.

options.A: Screen for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes now because overweight or obesity plus additional risk factors warrants testing even before age 35.
options.B: Wait until age 35 because risk factors do not change the age at which testing should begin.
options.C: Do not screen unless classic hyperglycemia symptoms develop because testing asymptomatic adults is not recommended.
options.D: Screen only if the client first develops hypertension because family history and physical inactivity are not recognized risk factors.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend risk assessment in asymptomatic adults and advise testing adults of any age who have overweight or obesity plus at least one additional risk factor. Recognized factors include a first-degree relative with diabetes and physical inactivity, among others. For people who do not otherwise meet risk-based criteria, routine screening begins at age 35. B incorrectly treats age 35 as a minimum regardless of risk. C and D ignore current risk-based screening guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA guidance supports diabetes testing before age 35 when an asymptomatic adult has overweight/obesity plus at least one recognized risk factor, including first-degree family history or physical inactivity.
candidate.source_document_title: Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Recommendations 2.11, 2.12a–2.12c and Table 2.5 — assess diabetes risk in asymptomatic adults; consider testing at any age in adults with overweight or obesity plus one or more risk factors including first-degree family history and physical inactivity; for all others screening begins at age 35
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: An asymptomatic 32-year-old adult has obesity, is physically inactive, and has a parent with type 2 diabetes. Which action best reflects current diabetes screening guidance?
